- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) and underestimate in bearish (sentiment < 0.3), especially after recent spikes.
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp price increases; reduce forecast by 5–10% in the 3–5 day window following a spike.
- Underreact to sustained negative sentiment; if sentiment remains below 0.3 for 3+ consecutive days, lower forecast by 3–7%.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show price decline, forecast should trend upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; adjust downward by 2–5% for first 7 days if sentiment is mixed or declining.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model overcorrects; reduce forecast by 3–6% to avoid “sentiment-driven overconfidence.”
